title: Blackstart home data
description: Shape reference for data/*.json. This documents the schema; scripts/validate.js is what actually enforces it (including the cross-field rules a JSON Schema cannot express, like poles matching slot count or estimatedWattsTotal matching its circuits).

schemaVersion.description: Bump only on a breaking change, and update Model.SCHEMA_VERSION to match.

backupSources.description: Keyed by an id that panels reference via backupSource.

maxOutputWatts.description: Instantaneous output ceiling. Governs how much at once. This is what the load check compares against.

cables.description: Cords that connect a backup source to a panel inlet, keyed by id and referenced from generatorInlet.cable. Keyed like backupSources so one cord serving two panels is described once.

ends.description: Which end is male and which is female. Spell it out.

howItConnects.description: Plain language, source end first. This is what someone reads while holding the cord in the dark.

equipment.description: Reference material about the hardware platform. Display-only; nothing computes from it.

panels.description: Keyed by panel id ("A", "B"). Device ids are prefixed with this key.

slots.description: Total positions. Odd = left column, even = right column.

generatorInlet.description: The backup feed. deviceId points at the device whose role is generatorInlet.

cable.description: Key into the top-level cables object. Both panels reference the same cord, so it is described once.

connection.description: What physically plugs in here. Called `connection`, not `receptacle`: this house's inlets are MALE flanged inlets, and calling one a receptacle is what caused a photo to be misread as needing a male-to-male cord.

gender.description: THE safety-relevant field. Male means a flanged inlet and an ordinary cord. Female means somebody needs a male-to-male cord with live exposed pins — the validator warns loudly if this is ever recorded as female.

genderVerified.description: Whether the gender was confirmed in person rather than read off a photo. The validator warns until it is true.

emptySlots.description: Slots VERIFIED to have no breaker. Declaring them is what lets the app tell 'empty' apart from 'nobody looked'. Any slot neither occupied nor listed here renders as 'Not surveyed'. A panel is fully surveyed when occupied + emptySlots = slots; that is derived, never stored.

devices.description: ONE ENTRY PER PHYSICAL BREAKER. A 2-pole breaker is one device with two slots, because it has one handle and trips as a unit.

id.description: Convention: <panel>-<slots joined by ->, e.g. A-9 or A-13-15. Stable; referenced by openQuestions and the UI.

slots.description: A 2-pole device occupies two same-parity slots two apart (both in one column), e.g. [13,15].

amps.description: The number on the handle. null for an installed device whose rating cannot be read yet — the key must still be present so the omission is deliberate. A null-amps device is absent from all load math.

role.description: Only 'branch' is a load. 'generatorInlet' is the backup feed and is excluded from search and all load math. 'feedThrough' is NOT a breaker: a plug-on lug that taps the bus, with no handle, no ampacity and no overcurrent protection of its own. It must have amps null, no circuits and no shedIn entries, and must name the subpanel it feeds via `feeds`. Its downstream load is charged to the panel as unsheddable.

feeds.description: feedThrough only. Id of the entry in subpanels[] that this device feeds. validate.js checks the subpanel points back at this device.

overcurrentProtection.description: feedThrough only. 'none' for a bare lug tap.

protectedBy.description: feedThrough only. What actually protects everything downstream, e.g. 'Panel B 200A main breaker only'.

equipment.description: The identified appliance on a single-purpose breaker. Display-only; nothing computes from it.

model.description: null when the unit is identified by make but the model was never read off it.

productUrl.description: Rendered as a real anchor in the app, so validate.js REQUIRES it to start with https:// — never let a javascript: or data: URI in through the data file. It will not open during an outage; it is provenance, not a feature.

label.description: What a non-technical person should read. Keep it short enough for a breaker tile.

shortLabel.description: Compact form for the printed panel-door insert, where a cell is about 32 characters wide. Falls back to `label`. scripts/make-insert.js reports any label that overflows rather than silently clipping it.

labelSource.description: Provenance. 'placeholder' or an 'auto-generated...' value makes validate.js warn until a human rewrites it.

physicalMarking.description: Anything written on or stuck to the breaker, e.g. 'orange tape'. Searchable.

physicalMarkingMeaning.description: What the marking MEANS, once someone knows. A mark whose meaning is unrecorded is a note to nobody: the orange tape here turned out to encode the outage shed list.

shedIn.description: Scenario keys in which this breaker gets turned off. THE single source of truth for shed lists — scenarios derive theirs from this.

photoVerified.description: False makes the UI badge this breaker as unverified.

circuits.description: What this breaker actually feeds. Empty array = breaker present, loads unknown (rendered differently from an empty slot).

fedFromSlot.description: Which of the device's own slots feeds this. A number for one leg of an MWBC, an array for a true 240V load.

notes.description: A STRING here (device-level notes is an array).

verified.description: Whether this circuit was actually confirmed at the panel. false makes the app badge it 'Unconfirmed' and show it as a guess. Absent means provenance was never recorded, which is different from recorded-and-failed.

verificationMethod.description: How it was confirmed, e.g. 'breaker walk-through'.

notes.description: An ARRAY here (circuit-level notes is a string).

estimatedWattsTotal.description: Must equal the sum of its circuits' estimatedWatts. validate.js enforces this.

subpanels.description: Enclosures downstream of a device in one of the panels — in practice, downstream of a feedThrough lug that no breaker in the parent panel can switch off. Their load IS counted against the parent panel's backup source, and is reported as unsheddable, because there is no handle upstream to throw.

id.description: Unique across devices too — validate.js checks for collisions.

location.description: Where the enclosure physically is. Load-bearing: a reader sweeping the parent panel needs to know this is somewhere else entirely.

deviceId.description: The device that feeds this. It must carry feeds: <this id>.

mainBreaker.description: null for a subpanel with no main. Pair that with disconnectArrangement so a reader can still tell how to kill power to it.

disconnectArrangement.description: Plain language: what actually disconnects this, given there may be no main.

feeder.description: The conductors between the parent panel and here. overcurrentProtection / protectedBy are the fields that matter when the tap is unfused.

devices.description: Breakers INSIDE this enclosure. They must NOT carry watts — watts live on appliances, or one appliance gets counted once per breaker feeding it. validate.js rejects estimatedWatts here.

position.description: null when the physical position was never recorded — which is a different claim from position 1.

serves.description: Appliance ids in this subpanel. Several breakers may serve ONE appliance; that is the multi-circuit heat kit case and it must not be summed per breaker.

appliances.description: What the subpanel actually feeds. THIS is where watts live. Appears in app search as rows flagged 'No breaker in Panel X'.

estimatedWatts.description: Total for the appliance, however many circuits feed it. null when unknown — the validator warns, because the subpanel total then reads low.

estimatedWattsTotal.description: Must equal the sum of its APPLIANCES' estimatedWatts (nulls excluded). validate.js enforces this.

openQuestions.description: Known unknowns and contradictions. deviceIds link a question to breakers so the UI can badge disputed data instead of presenting it as settled.

subpanelId.description: Optional link to an entry in subpanels[], for questions about something downstream of a tap rather than about a breaker.

panels.description: Panels this warning applies to. OMIT for warnings that apply everywhere. Scoping matters on the printed per-panel inserts: without it the Panel B card carried the Anker trickle-charge instruction, which is a Panel A device.

walkthroughSteps.description: Keyed by procedure: panelA, panelB, rechargeAnkerFromTruck.

icon.description: Name from the icon map in src/app.js. Unknown names fall back to the step number.

breakersToTurnOff.description: 'scenario-dependent' resolves from devices[].shedIn for this step's panel.

lastUpdated.description: Shown in the app so a reader knows how fresh the offline copy is.

unassignedEndpoints.description: Endpoints known to exist whose breaker has not been identified. These ARE shown in search, as rows reading 'Breaker unknown' — omitting them would imply the outlet does not exist. Once traced, move the entry into that device's circuits and delete it here.

monitoring.description: Whether this branch can ever be metered by a smart breaker. Load reaching an enclosure through a feed-through lug never passes a branch breaker, so no amount of breaker swapping instruments it.

instrumentationPath.description: What WOULD work, e.g. 'a CT pair on the feeder'.
